description: Server-sent-event framing for /v1/chat/streams. Joi frames this stream itself on every platform instead of using a line-reading convenience API, because the common ones do not emit empty lines — and an empty line is exactly what terminates an SSE frame. Using one concatenates consecutive events into a single invalid payload, which unit tests over hand-written single frames do not catch and a live stream fails on every turn.
notes: The runner concatenates `chunks` (UTF-8) or `chunksBase64` into one byte sequence and feeds it to the framer one byte at a time, collecting each payload the framer emits, then flushes the stream end. Chunk boundaries carry no meaning: they exist so a case can place a boundary somewhere hostile.
`payloads` is the exact ordered list of `data:` payloads the framer must emit. Multi-line data is joined with a single U+000A.

`id:` and `event:` lines are read and discarded: the payload itself carries the authoritative event, request and thread identity, so retaining a transport-level id would create a second, weaker source of truth.
A frame whose accumulated data payload is empty produces no event at all rather than an empty one.
Contractual but not vectored, because the literal case would be half a megabyte: a single line longer than 512 KiB is a malformed stream, not something to buffer without bound.

cases.note: The regression that motivated an owned framer. A line reader that drops empty lines returns one payload here — the two objects glued together — and every turn fails as malformed.
The CR belongs to the delimiter, not to the payload.
A comment line is not blank, so it must not close the frame.
An empty payload is not an event.
Exactly one space after the colon is grammar; any further space is payload.
A network chunk boundary is not a token boundary.
The boundary falls inside the three bytes of U+8BF4. A framer that decodes each chunk to text as it arrives corrupts the character here; one that decodes at the line boundary does not.
A complete final frame is still delivered when the connection ends without its terminating blank line.
The truncated trailing line contributes nothing, but the data already accumulated for that frame is still delivered.
A truncated `data:` line is indistinguishable from a complete one at the transport layer. It is delivered, and the payload's own JSON validity is what rejects it.
